sections.title: Form and nomenclature
sections.text: Common medlar is a thorny shrub or small deciduous tree about 3–6 m tall, native to south-western Asia and south-eastern Europe. The catalogue retains the name Mespilus germanica; Kew treats it as a synonym of Crataegus germanica.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: The solitary white flowers are about 3–5 cm across. The brown fruits have a broad open end surrounded by five persistent sepals.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Medlar fruits are eaten after bletting, when the flesh has softened. Hard, unbletted fruits are very astringent.
